purpose: Persistent source registry and completeness contract for the Trentino event database.
coverageWindow: rolling 12 months from each scan date

rules: Use search engines only for source discovery; never treat search-result snippets as a complete scan of a known event calendar.
For every P0/P1 calendar, start from its event index and enumerate all pages, load-more results, date buckets, category tabs and child links that fall in the rolling window.

Record the source-reported total when available and reconcile it against unique records seen. A scan is COMPLETE only when pagination/end-of-results is reached and the count is reconciled or the source has no count.
Follow linked PDFs, brochures, downloadable calendars, flyers and attachments. Extract every separately named dated event or recurring series in scope.

Expand 'other available dates', recurring weekday patterns and series pages. Store one canonical series with recurrence metadata when the event identity is the same; store separate records when individual occurrences have distinct names/programmes.
Open detail pages for date, venue, municipality, organizer, price, image and cancellation/status verification.
Never silently skip long-running exhibitions, weekly markets, guided visits, family programmes, small local events or events that are not labelled Top Event.
A source that times out, blocks access, changes pagination, or cannot be fully traversed must be logged PARTIAL or FAILED; do not mark the overall run fully complete.
Deduplicate only after discovery. Preserve the strongest official/public URL and list corroborating sources when useful.
Add newly discovered recurring sources, organizer calendars and public social accounts to this registry so coverage grows over time.

rules: Search public posts/pages for tourism boards, municipalities, Pro Loco groups, museums, venues, organisers and associations.
When a flyer or social post contains a valid date/location and no official calendar record exists yet, add it as an unconfirmed/public-source event and continue looking for corroboration.
Do not use inaccessible/private social content as evidence and do not infer missing dates from images that cannot be read reliably.
A social-only event must not be treated as cancelled merely because the post later becomes unavailable.

completionGate.userFacingRule: If any P0 source is PARTIAL or FAILED, surface a coverage warning even when there are no event changes.
